# CDP reference

Every query kind and command: **What** it answers (and does not), **How** to call it (parameters, defaults, examples), **Where** it fits (which question, what next). Same text as `cdp help <topic>` and the MCP `cdp_help` tool.

## Which kind for which question

| Question | kind |
|---|---|
| how does X work / what do I read / what breaks if X changes | `trace` |
| where is X defined / who calls X | `symbol` |
| what is in this file | `file` |
| what does module M do / depend on | `module` |
| what endpoints exist | `routes` |
| who reads/writes table T; which tables does a route touch | `table` |
| where is config key / env var K read | `config` |
| how does data get from A to B | `paths` |
| what do we not know / what should a human answer | `unknowns` |
| what do we claim about X; list all entrypoints/dependencies | `claims` |
| is anything contradictory | `conflicts` |
| shape of the repo; did the scan cover it | `stats` |
| is it safe to say 'there is no X' | `coverage` |
| none of the above | `search` |

## Query parameters

| MCP param | CLI flag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `term` | `<term>` | the name this kind looks up (see each kind) |
| `budget` | `--budget` | row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped |
| `exclude_role` | `--exclude-role` | drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable |
| `claim_kind` | `--kind` | `claims`: only claims of this kind |
| `module` | `--module` | `claims`: only claims whose module contains this text |
| `subject` | `--subject` | `claims`: only claims whose subject contains this text |
| `frm` | `--from` | `paths`: paths through any node containing this text (with `to`, it must come first) |
| `to` | `--to` | `paths`: paths through any node containing this text (with `frm`, it must come after) |
| `exact` | `--exact` | `symbol`/`file`/`routes`/`table`/`config`: match the whole name instead of a case-insensitive substring; the answer's `match` says which was used |
| `max_hops` | `--max-hops` | `trace`: how many edges to walk (default 8) |
| `as_of` | `--as-of` | replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current |

Which kinds take which parameter:

| kind | parameters |
|---|---|
| `trace` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `max_hops`, `as_of` |
| `symbol` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `exact`, `as_of` |
| `file` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `exact`, `as_of` |
| `module` | `term`, `budget`, `as_of` |
| `routes` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `exact`, `as_of` |
| `table` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `exact`, `as_of` |
| `config` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `exact`, `as_of` |
| `paths` | `frm`, `to`, `budget`, `as_of` |
| `search` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `as_of` |
| `claims` | `term`, `claim_kind`, `module`, `subject`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `as_of` |
| `unknowns` | `term`, `budget`, `exclude_role`, `as_of` |
| `conflicts` | `budget`, `as_of` |
| `stats` | `as_of` |
| `coverage` | `as_of` |

## Query kinds

### `trace` -- reading list for an entry point: every file on its call chain, cited

**What.** The minimal cited file set needed to understand an entry point: the files its call/persist/publish edges reach (including the `@Subscribe` handlers of an EventBus event it posts), each with the edge that put it there.

- Limits: Not logic: no parameters or branches. DI/reflection wiring leaves no edge, so a short trail is not proof of 'calls nothing'. Edges tagged `medium` come from imports or interface/override fan-out (can reach, not does). A class term (`TenantController`) is not one entry point: each public member is walked and the list is capped at 40 files (round-robin, nearest first; the cap and the unlisted count are stated, and `--budget` does not lift it) - trace a member or a route for a whole chain.
- Reading it: `resolved_as` says what the term matched (route, source or symbol); `files` are the reading list in walk order; `hops_exhausted` true means raise --max-hops; `elided: 0` means the list is complete. A route path shared by several verbs is traced for every verb (`verbs`; a file only some verbs reach is tagged `(POST only)`). The entry point (`resolved_as`) and each hop row that cites one definition (`defines X`) carry that symbol's annotations (verbatim text + `file:line`), annotated parameters and owner-class annotations; a hop with no single cited symbol shows none.

**How.** `term`: REQUIRED. A route path (`/orders`; all its verbs) or `VERB /path` (`POST /orders`; one), a dataflow source, a class (`OrderResource`: its public members) or a member (`OrderResource#place`); substring, first match wins in that order.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `max_hops` (`--max-hops`): `trace`: how many edges to walk (default 8)
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query trace <route>
    $ cdp query trace <method> --max-hops 4 --exclude-role test

**Where.** Start here for 'how does X work / what do I read / what breaks if I change X'. Next: Read only the cited line ranges; `symbol` on a hop for its callers; `table`/`config` for what the chain persists or reads.

### `symbol` -- definition site(s) and every use of a class/method (callers)

**What.** Where a class, method or constant is defined (with line extent) and every site that uses it: the transpose of the resolved import and call tables.

- Limits: Not dynamic dispatch, reflection or DI wiring. `used_by` of an interface lists its implementers' callers only where the call resolves. A class's `used_by` includes its `new X(..)` sites (an implicit default constructor counts as the class). Java: a call on a type variable resolves through its declared bound(s) only; an inferred generic method result (`<T> T pick()`) stays untyped. C#: `x.M()`, `new X(..)`, `new(..)`, `: base(..)`, method groups and extension methods resolve through declared types, `var`, `await`, collections/LINQ and explicit `M<T>()` arguments; a lambda parameter is typed only for LINQ-style stages and Moq `Setup`/`Verify`; overloads share one symbol and are told apart only by argument count (an interface method can win over an extension of the same name), and a NuGet-typed receiver leaves no edge. Python: calls, references, decorators and `from x import f` resolve for `f()`, `self.m()`, `mod.f()`, `Class(..)` (to `__init__`), and `obj.m()` only when `obj`'s class is known (`self`, annotation, `x = Class()`, a callee's annotated/inferred return, isinstance); an untyped parameter's calls, `getattr`, dispatch through a list of modules and decorator-built wrappers are not found.
- Reading it: `defined_range` is `file:start-end` (read exactly that); `used_by_count` is the true total even when the list is budgeted (several matches split the budget evenly, and a cut one gives `see_all`, the exact command for every use); `collision` true means several definitions share the name. Each definition also shows its annotations (verbatim text + `file:line`), annotated parameters and the owner class's annotations (Java).

**How.** `term`: REQUIRED. Fully-qualified name, a suffix (`OrderService`), or `Class#method`; case-insensitive substring (exact last-name matches first) unless `exact`; `Class#method` is always exact.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `exact` (`--exact`): `symbol`/`file`/`routes`/`table`/`config`: match the whole name instead of a case-insensitive substring; the answer's `match` says which was used
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query symbol <symbol>
    $ cdp query symbol <method> --exclude-role test

**Where.** 'Where is X defined / who calls X / who uses X'. Prefer over grep. Next: `trace` from a caller or `file` for the defining file's outline.

### `file` -- what one file defines and touches (outline)

**What.** One file's module, language, role, LOC, every definition with line extent, and its I/O edges (tables, config, HTTP, events).

- Limits: Not file contents. Use it to pick the line range to Read.
- Reading it: `defines` is the outline with `line`..`end_line`; `io_edges` are what the file reads/writes/calls out to. Each definition lists its annotations (verbatim text + `file:line`), annotated parameters and the owner class's annotations (Java).

**How.** `term`: REQUIRED. A repo-relative path or any substring of one (`exact`: the path or a trailing `dir/file`); an absolute path inside another scanned repo is routed to that repo's store.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `exact` (`--exact`): `symbol`/`file`/`routes`/`table`/`config`: match the whole name instead of a case-insensitive substring; the answer's `match` says which was used
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query file <file>

**Where.** 'What does this file do / what is in it' -- before opening it. Next: Read the cited ranges; `symbol` on a definition for its users.

### `module` -- one build module: size, dependencies, dependents, claims

**What.** A build module's files, LOC, languages, roles, what it depends on and who depends on it (observed vs declared), its scopes and claim tally.

- Limits: Not per-file detail (use `file`). `exclude_role` does not apply.
- Reading it: `declared_only` = in the build file but never imported; `observed_only` = imported but undeclared.

**How.** `term`: REQUIRED. Module name or substring.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query module <module>

**Where.** 'What does module M do / depend on / who depends on it'. Next: `file` for one of its files; `stats` for the module list.

### `routes` -- the HTTP surface: verb, path, handler, citation

**What.** Every HTTP route with verb, path (constants resolved; a Dropwizard module's `server.applicationContextPath` prefixed), handler and the annotation/constant sites that declare it.

- Limits: Not outbound HTTP calls; not routes built at runtime. Unresolved constants are listed, not guessed.
- Reading it: `declared_via` shows the constant expression; `unresolved_constants` non-empty means the path is partial. Each route also shows its handler's annotations (verbatim text + `file:line`), annotated parameters and owner-class annotations, a few lines per route (`--json` has all).

**How.** `term`: OPTIONAL. Substring of the route path, the verb, `VERB /path` or the handler class/method (`/orders`, `POST`, `OrderResource`; each row's `matched_via` says which); `exact` matches the whole name; omit for all.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `exact` (`--exact`): `symbol`/`file`/`routes`/`table`/`config`: match the whole name instead of a case-insensitive substring; the answer's `match` says which was used
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query routes
    $ cdp query routes <route>

**Where.** 'What endpoints exist / which handler serves /x'. Next: `trace <route>` for everything the endpoint reaches.

### `table` -- who owns (migration), writes and reads a database table

**What.** Per table: owning module and migration DDL, writers, readers, each with a citation. The union is 'what breaks if I change this table'.

- Limits: Only tables seen in migrations or persistence/read code; not raw SQL in strings the extractor cannot parse.
- Reading it: `migrations` = schema owner; `writers`/`readers` group the sites by who touches the table (SQL scripts are one group: site and file counts, a few `file:line`); `entity_users` are the uses of the entity class outside the DbContext and migrations (reads and writes not told apart); `evidence` is the cited sites. Each code writer/reader group shows its annotations (verbatim text + `file:line`), annotated parameters and owner-class annotations (e.g. `@Table(name=..)`); script groups show none.

**How.** `term`: OPTIONAL. Substring of the table name (`order` also matches `orders`) unless `exact`; omit for all.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `exact` (`--exact`): `symbol`/`file`/`routes`/`table`/`config`: match the whole name instead of a case-insensitive substring; the answer's `match` says which was used
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query table
    $ cdp query table <table>

**Where.** 'Who writes/reads table T', 'which tables does X touch' (with `trace`). Next: `symbol` on a writer; `trace` from the route that reaches it.

### `config` -- config keys and env vars: where declared, every site that reads them

**What.** Each config key / env var with its declarations, values and read sites (config files, Docker `ENV`, `${VAR:-default}` placeholders, Python (`os.environ[..]`/`.get`, `os.getenv`, `environ`/`getenv` imports, keys held in constants, `django.conf.settings.X`, pydantic `BaseSettings` fields)/JS/Go env reads, Java `System.getenv`/`getProperty`/`Long.getLong`/`getenv().getOrDefault`, `@Value`; C# `IConfiguration` indexer/`GetValue`/`GetSection`/`GetConnectionString`, `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable`, `appsettings*.json` keys as `A:B`).

- Limits: Not values set outside the repo (deploy-time env). A key built at run time is listed under `(dynamic)`, not by name. Java reads through a provider (`configProvider.getValue(KEY)`, `env.getProperty("k")`) and calls to wrapper methods that pass a literal/constant key on to `System.getenv`/a provider are found; a provider whose type and names never mention config/properties/env, or a wrapper reached only through an interface, is not.
- Reading it: `declared` vs `read` sites; `values` are the literal defaults seen. Keys are ranked by read sites; `read_count` is the true total, `keys_elided`/`sites_elided` count what the budget cut (raise `budget` or pass a term to see every site). Each read site shows its reader's annotations (verbatim text + `file:line`), annotated parameters and owner-class annotations.

**How.** `term`: OPTIONAL. Substring of the key name (`MINI_DB`, `billing.url`; `exact`: whole key); omit for all keys (most-read first, a few citations each; pass a term to see every site).

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `exact` (`--exact`): `symbol`/`file`/`routes`/`table`/`config`: match the whole name instead of a case-insensitive substring; the answer's `match` says which was used
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query config <config-key>

**Where.** 'Where is setting K read / what does the service read from env'. Next: `symbol` on a reader; `file` for the declaring file.

### `paths` -- traced dataflow paths from a source to a sink (A -> B)

**What.** End-to-end paths (trigger, hops with channel and citation) between a source and a sink, e.g. route -> service -> repository -> table.

- Limits: Only paths the dataflow graph closed; 0 paths does not mean unconnected. Nodes are classes, so `Class#method` matches the class.
- Reading it: `hops` in order, each `--channel--> node  file:line`; `confidence` is the weakest hop.

**How.** `term`: NOT USED: pass `frm`/`to` (CLI `--from`/`--to`).

- `frm` (`--from`): `paths`: paths through any node containing this text (with `to`, it must come first)
- `to` (`--to`): `paths`: paths through any node containing this text (with `frm`, it must come after)
- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query paths --from <route>
    $ cdp query paths --from <route> --to <table>

**Where.** 'How does data get from A to B' -- when A and B are an entry point and a sink. Next: `trace` when 0 paths (walks edges without needing a closed path).

### `search` -- free-text fallback across claims, symbols, constants, unknowns and files

**What.** Substring search over claim subjects/statements, symbol names, constant values, unknown questions and file paths, ranked by closeness.

- Limits: Not file contents (that is grep); an empty answer says what was and was not searched.
- Reading it: `counts` are true totals; each list is budget-split fairly. An `annotations` bucket matches annotation name, fqn, verbatim text and argument values, whitespace ignored (`search @Every`, `search 60s`); rows are `owner  @text  file:line`.

**How.** `term`: REQUIRED. Any text.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query search <word>

**Where.** Only when no specific kind fits. Prefer symbol/file/table/config/routes. Next: Re-ask with the specific kind on a hit.

### `claims` -- reviewed claims, filtered by kind, module or subject

**What.** The claim log: structural facts and model/human claims with confidence and evidence anchors.

- Limits: Deterministic scans yield few claims; no model review means few interpretive ones (see `coverage`).
- Reading it: `confidence` and `verdict` per claim; every claim has evidence `file:line`.

**How.** `term`: OPTIONAL shorthand for `claim_kind`; do not combine with a different `claim_kind`.

- `claim_kind` (`--kind`): `claims`: only claims of this kind
- `module` (`--module`): `claims`: only claims whose module contains this text
- `subject` (`--subject`): `claims`: only claims whose subject contains this text
- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query claims --kind entrypoint
    $ cdp query claims --subject <symbol>

**Where.** 'What do we claim about X / list all entrypoints/dependencies'. Next: `symbol`/`file` for context on a claim's subject.

### `unknowns` -- what the index could not determine, with what would resolve it

**What.** Open questions grouped by scope node, each with `needs_*` describing what would resolve it.

- Limits: Completeness of unknowns is unknowable; it lists what was noticed.
- Reading it: Grouped by `source_node`; resolve with `answer`.

**How.** `term`: OPTIONAL. Filter to scope nodes containing this text (`root/web`).

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `exclude_role` (`--exclude-role`): drop rows whose file has these roles (test, build, ci, config, docs, asset, schema, source); repeatable
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query unknowns
    $ cdp query unknowns <module>

**Where.** 'What don't we know / what should I ask a human'. Next: `cdp answer` to record the human answer.

### `conflicts` -- claims that contradict each other, plus near-misses

**What.** Subjects where two claims disagree, and near-misses that almost merged.

- Limits: Only conflicts between recorded claims.
- Reading it: `count` conflicts, `near_miss_count` near-misses.

**How.** `term`: NOT USED.

- `budget` (`--budget`): row cap across every list in the answer (default 200); `elided: N` reports what was dropped
- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query conflicts

**Where.** 'Is anything contradictory / which facts are contested'. Next: `claims --subject <s>` for both sides.

### `stats` -- census: files, languages, modules, symbols, routes, claims, coverage

**What.** Whole-repo counts, the head commit, resolution rates and declared-vs-observed module dependency divergence.

- Limits: Counts only; never budgeted and never filtered (so it is a safe first call).
- Reading it: `resolution` = how many imports resolved; `coverage.fraction` < 1 means absence in other answers is 'not examined'.

**How.** `term`: NOT USED.

- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query stats

**Where.** First call on an unfamiliar repo: shape and module list. Next: `routes`, `module <m>`, `trace <entry>`.

### `coverage` -- what fraction of tracked files was examined, and what was skipped

**What.** Coverage fraction, per-node status, skipped files and node errors.

- Limits: Never budgeted or filtered.
- Reading it: `warning` set means every absence elsewhere is 'unexamined', not 'absent'.

**How.** `term`: NOT USED.

- `as_of` (`--as-of`): replay the claim log up to this commit (sha); structure stays current

    $ cdp query coverage

**Where.** Before saying 'there is no X'. Next: `stats`; `status` for freshness.

## Commands

### `scan`

**What.** Deterministic extraction of the whole repo (symbols, call edges, routes, tables, config, dataflow, claims). No model calls. Writes the machine store and, unless `--no-docs`, the markdown docs. State lives in ONE machine store, `CDP_HOME` (default `~/.cdp`), never in the repo: index in `index.db`, files under `work/<repo-slug>/` (`docs/`, `prompts/`, `patches/inbox/`).

**How.** Re-running is safe (new snapshot at the current commit). Indexes the working tree as is: with uncommitted edits the snapshot is labelled `+uncommitted`. `--max-leaf-files`/`--max-leaf-loc` size the scopes `prompts` hands to leaf agents; `--max-concurrent` caps scopes per wave; `--max-hops` caps dataflow path length; `--workers 1` forces sequential extraction.

    $ cdp scan
    $ cdp scan --exclude vendor --workers 4
    $ cdp scan --no-docs --quiet

**Where.** First command on any repo, or after structural changes. Then `query stats`.

### `query`

**What.** Ask the index a typed question; every answer is cited `file:line` and carries `as_of`. 14 kinds, see `help <kind>`. Read-only.

**How.** `query <kind> [term]`. Parameters apply per kind; passing one a kind does not use is an error. `--budget` caps rows (default 200; `elided: N` reports the cut); `stats` and `coverage` are never budgeted. `--json` prints the full result.

    $ cdp query stats --json
    $ cdp query symbol <symbol> --as-of <sha>

**Where.** Everything about the code. Pick the kind with `help recipes` or the table in `help`.

### `docs`

**What.** Renders `00-overview.md`, `modules/<module>.md`, `dataflow.md`, `unknowns.md`, `CLAUDE.md` from the index. Read-only on the index.

**How.** Default output `<CDP_HOME>/work/<repo-slug>/docs/` (printed). `--out DIR` writes elsewhere.

    $ cdp docs
    $ cdp docs --out <out>

**Where.** Onboarding or a CLAUDE.md draft. For a specific question use `query`.

### `status`

**What.** Index head vs git HEAD (behind/dirty), coverage, freshness buckets, waves, per-node status and the current run's task table.

**How.** `--json` is what the SessionStart hook and MCP `cdp_status` read. Answers come from the snapshot of HEAD, else the nearest clean ancestor, never another branch (else `scan`); `N uncommitted file(s) included in this index` = a `+uncommitted` snapshot.

    $ cdp status
    $ cdp status --json

**Where.** Before trusting an answer as current. Behind -> `refresh`; stale -> `run --stale-only`.

### `diff`

**What.** Typed structural deltas (files added/removed/changed, symbols added/removed/changed, routes, module edges, claims) between two scanned snapshots of the same repo. A file counts as changed when its size, line count or a definition's extent differs (no content hash is kept).

**How.** Two forms: `diff <old_state> <new_state>` (two state directories) or `diff --old-sha A --new-sha B` (snapshots of `--repo`; needs the sqlite/postgres store). An omitted side defaults to the current/latest scanned snapshot; both omitted compares a snapshot with itself. Git file changes without a re-scan do not appear.

    $ cdp diff --old-sha <sha> --new-sha <sha>
    $ cdp diff <old_state> <new_state>

**Where.** 'What changed structurally between releases'. Then `query symbol`/`table` on an item.

### `prompts`

**What.** Writes one leaf prompt per scope for the optional model-review layer.

**How.** Output `<CDP_HOME>/work/<repo-slug>/prompts/<node>.md` (printed). `--wave N`/`--node X` limit it; `--digest` builds full-file prompts instead of citation prompts; `--measure` prints token estimates and writes nothing; `--lessons N`/`--no-lessons` choose the lesson-set.

    $ cdp prompts
    $ cdp prompts --wave 0 --digest
    $ cdp prompts --measure

**Where.** Only for model review. Hand each prompt to a leaf, drop its patch in `<CDP_HOME>/work/<repo-slug>/patches/inbox/`, then `collect`.

### `collect`

**What.** Validates, verifies (anchors exist), entails and appends the leaf patches in the inbox.

**How.** Reads `<CDP_HOME>/work/<repo-slug>/patches/inbox/`. `--mode strict` (default) demotes unverifiable claims to unknowns; `lenient` keeps more.

    $ cdp collect

**Where.** After leaves wrote patches. Then `fold --check`.

### `fold`

**What.** Recomputes `state.json` (claims, unknowns, coverage) from the patch log + xref.

**How.** `--check` verifies the invariant and writes nothing.

    $ cdp fold
    $ cdp fold --check

**Where.** After `collect`/`rollback`/`compact`. Failure of `--check` -> `rollback` the run, then `fold`.

### `refresh`

**What.** Incremental update: re-extracts changed files, re-verifies every live claim against HEAD, no model calls. No-op when HEAD is unchanged.

**How.** `--quiet` for hooks. Run automatically at session start; `githook install` runs it on commit. Refuses a dirty tree (`refresh requires a clean working tree`, exit 2): commit, stash, or `scan` (which indexes it as `+uncommitted`).

    $ cdp refresh
    $ cdp refresh --quiet

**Where.** Index is behind HEAD. Then `status`.

### `run`

**What.** The wave loop for model review: dispatch leaves -> collect -> adjudicate -> fold, supervised (leases, retries, resume). Costs model calls via `--runner-cmd`.

**How.** Target: `--wave N`, `--wave-all`, `--stale-only` or `--scope NODE`. Without `--runner-cmd` it waits for patches dropped by hand. `--parallel N` runs N scopes of a wave at once; `--timeout` (default 900s) and `--max-attempts` (3) bound a scope; `--resume` continues an interrupted run.

    $ cdp run --wave-all --runner-cmd "<cmd>" --parallel 4
    $ cdp run --stale-only --runner-cmd "<cmd>"
    $ cdp run --resume --wave-all

**Where.** Optional: adds meaning on top of `scan`. `status` shows task state.

### `verify`

**What.** Recomputes the fold from the log and diffs it with `state.json`; `--full` also proves the cold archive.

**How.** Read-only. `--mode` as in `collect`.

    $ cdp verify
    $ cdp verify --full

**Where.** Integrity check. FAIL -> `rollback --to-run <run>`, then `fold`.

### `answer`

**What.** Records a human claim against an unknown through the same validate/verify/entail/fold pipeline as a leaf patch (`author_kind=human`).

**How.** `answer <scope> --subject S --kind K --claim TEXT --anchor FILE:LINE`; the scope is the node (`root/web`, see `query unknowns`). Exit 1 if verification demoted the claim. `--channel`, `--confidence`, `--author`, `--mode` are optional.

    $ cdp answer root --subject <symbol> --kind ownership --claim "Owned by orders team" --anchor <file>:1

**Where.** After `query unknowns` lists something a human knows. Then `query unknowns` again.

### `reflect`

**What.** One model call per outlier scope from a run's trajectory corpus; keeps well-formed promotions.

**How.** `--runner-cmd` required; `--limit` scopes (default 5); `--run-id` defaults to the store's run.

    $ cdp reflect --runner-cmd "<cmd>" --limit 3

**Where.** After a `run`. Then `lessons cut`.

### `lessons`

**What.** Cut and inspect numbered, pinned lesson-sets.

**How.** `lessons cut`; `lessons show [--version N]`; `lessons unpromote --version N --reason TEXT`.

    $ cdp lessons cut
    $ cdp lessons show

**Where.** After `reflect`. Then `holdout --lessons N` before trusting a cut.

### `holdout`

**What.** A/B a lesson-set cut on a repo outside its own learning corpus; promotes it to latest only if tiering does not regress.

**How.** `holdout --lessons N --repo <holdout-repo>`: the holdout repo is `--repo`, not a positional. Exit 1 on reject.

    $ cdp holdout --lessons 1 --repo <repo>

**Where.** After `lessons cut`. On promote: `run` uses it by default.

### `gc`

**What.** Drops snapshots not kept by retention (HEAD, pinned, cited by a live claim).

**How.** `--dry-run` reports only; `--pin SHA`/`--unpin SHA` mark snapshots before computing; `--head-sha` overrides HEAD; `--db PATH` targets another existing store. SHAs may be unique prefixes; an ambiguous one lists the candidates.

    $ cdp gc --dry-run
    $ cdp gc --pin <sha> --dry-run

**Where.** Disk pressure. Then `compact` for superseded patches.

### `compact`

**What.** Moves superseded patch generations to the cold archive.

**How.** `--keep-generations N` (default 1; keep >= 1), `--compact-threshold F` (default 0.30), `--dry-run`. Run `fold` and `verify` afterwards.

    $ cdp compact --dry-run
    $ cdp compact --keep-generations 2

**Where.** Large patch logs. `export --format archive` inspects what moved.

### `export`

**What.** Dumps the store: canonical `json`, reviewable `patches`, cold `archive`, or an `anonymized` corpus.

**How.** `--out DIR` (required). `--format` default `json`. `--db PATH` exports another store.

    $ cdp export --format json --out <out>
    $ cdp export --format patches --out <out>

**Where.** Backup, review, or sharing a corpus.

### `rollback`

**What.** Excludes a run's patches from the fold without deleting them (append-only ledger); `--undo` reverses the latest.

**How.** `--to-run RUN` excludes one run; `--to-snapshot SHA` that run and every later one; `--reason` is recorded.

    $ cdp rollback --to-run <run> --reason "bad batch"
    $ cdp rollback --undo

**Where.** `verify`/`fold --check` fails, or a bad batch of claims. Then `query stats`.

### `doctor`

**What.** Conformance harness for a model: schema validity, anchor survival, entailment, recall against a golden set. Writes `<CDP_HOME>/doctor/<model>.json`.

**How.** `--runner-cmd` and `--model` required; `--node` limits scopes; `--timeout` 300s.

    $ cdp doctor --runner-cmd "<cmd>" --model my-model

**Where.** Before trusting a new model as a leaf.

### `validate`

**What.** Validates a patch file against the patch schema.

**How.** Read-only. A non-JSON file is an error.

    $ cdp validate <patch.json>

**Where.** Debugging a leaf's output before `collect`.

### `githook`

**What.** Installs/removes git `post-commit`, `post-checkout`, `post-merge` and `post-rewrite` hooks running `cdp refresh` (commit, branch switch, pull, rebase).

**How.** Writes only into the repo's hooks directory, all four or none (a foreign hook of the same name refuses the whole install); one install serves every worktree; `uninstall` removes only CDP's hooks. Works from a checkout of CDP (no PYTHONPATH needed).

    $ cdp githook install
    $ cdp githook uninstall

**Where.** Keep the index fresh on every commit, pull and rebase. (`install --harness` is the Claude Code session setup, not this.)

### `install`

**What.** Copies the skill into another repo (`.claude/skills/cdp`, plus the `cdp-leaf` agent; runtime files only, no `tests/`, ~0.5 MB). Nothing else is written by default; `--harness` adds Claude Code hooks and `.mcp.json`.

**How.** `install <target>`; `--framework {claude-code,langgraph,adk,none}`; `--hook` adds the PreToolUse nudge; `--harness` = the nudge (never blocks; it names the exact `cdp_query` for the Grep/Glob/Read the model reached for, once per subject, quiet after the first `cdp_query`) + UserPromptSubmit (names the kind for the question) + SessionStart refresh/status + a PostToolUse hint after empty searches + MCP server; `--strict` swaps the nudge for the gate (a repo-wide grep/find or whole-file Read the index fully answers is denied once with the answer, everything else runs; any `cdp_query` switches it off for the session); `--claude-md` writes a marked `MUST use cdp_query first` block (generated from this guide) into the target's CLAUDE.md, creating the file, never touching text outside the markers; `--allow-mcp` adds `mcp__cdp__*` to `permissions.allow` (the cdp tools run without a prompt; they edit no repository files); `--priority` = `--harness --strict --claude-md --allow-mcp`, the CDP-first preset; `--agents-md` also writes AGENTS.md; headless `claude -p` refuses MCP tools unless allowed (`--allowedTools "mcp__cdp__*"` or `--allow-mcp`); `--remove-harness` undoes hooks, the MCP entry, the CLAUDE.md block and the permission (only what install added) and deletes settings files it leaves empty; `--self` refreshes this repo's vendored copy (for CDP developers).

    $ cdp install <target>
    $ cdp install <target> --harness
    $ cdp install <target> --priority
    $ cdp install <target> --remove-harness

**Where.** Once per repo you want Claude to use CDP in. Then `scan --repo <target>`.

### `selftest`

**What.** Runs the bundled tests, or the reproducibility (`--determinism REPO`) / golden (`--golden`) gates.

**How.** `--min-tests N` fails if fewer ran; `--bless` with `--golden` overwrites the baseline.

    $ cdp selftest --min-tests 100

**Where.** From a CDP checkout, to prove it works (an installed copy has no `tests/`: use `selftest --determinism REPO` there).

### `help`

**What.** This guide: every command and query kind with What / How / Where, generated from one source.

**How.** `help` overview; `help <command>`; `help <kind>`; `help recipes`; `help reference` (the full reference); `--json` machine-readable. MCP: `cdp_help`.

    $ cdp help
    $ cdp help query
    $ cdp help trace
    $ cdp help recipes

**Where.** Whenever you are unsure which command or flag to use.

### `link`

**What.** Cross-repo/module edges: which service calls which, what publishes to a topic, matched across scanned repos. Subcommands: `scan`, `query`, `prompts`, `collect`, `run`, `refresh`.

**How.** `link scan` (no args: every repo in the machine store at its latest snapshot; or stand-alone state dirs) matches channel edges -- HTTP client calls (Refit, HttpClient, requests, fetch, Feign, RestTemplate) to server routes -- and does not modify the index (it takes the one empty `locks/links-*.lock` file, reused, and SQLite may touch `index.db-shm`); `link scan --db` saves the links. `link query --service NAME` (repo directory name, path, identity or unique prefix) lists callers and unmatched calls (unknown name: error listing the known ones). Over MCP: `cdp_link`. Ambiguous matches go through `link prompts --out DIR` -> leaf -> `link collect --in DIR`, or `link run --runner-cmd` (one step). `link refresh` re-verifies after a re-scan.

    $ cdp link scan
    $ cdp link scan --db
    $ cdp link scan --db <db>
    $ cdp link query --service <repo-name> --db <db>
    $ cdp link prompts --out <out> --db <db>
    $ cdp link collect --in <out> --db <db>
    $ cdp link run --db <db>
    $ cdp link refresh --db <db>

**Where.** 'Who calls this service / what breaks in other repos'. Scan every repo first.

## Recipes

### Who calls X

_You need the callers of a class or method._

    $ cdp query symbol <symbol>
    $ cdp query trace <method>

`symbol` lists definition sites and every `used_by` site, cited. `trace` shows what X reaches.

### What breaks if I change Y

_Before editing a method, route or table._

    $ cdp query trace <route> --exclude-role test
    $ cdp query symbol <method>
    $ cdp query table <table>

`trace` is the reading list downstream; `symbol` the callers upstream; `table` every writer/reader. Read only the cited ranges.

### Which tables does a route touch

_Mapping an endpoint to its storage._

    $ cdp query routes <route>
    $ cdp query paths --from <route>
    $ cdp query table

`paths` shows route -> service -> repository -> table when the path closes; if it reports 0 paths use `trace <route>`.

### Where is a config key read

_Finding the code behind a setting or env var._

    $ cdp query config <config-key>
    $ cdp query file <file>

`config` gives declarations and every read site; `file` outlines the reader.

### Onboard onto an unfamiliar repository

_First contact with a repo._

    $ cdp scan
    $ cdp query stats
    $ cdp query routes
    $ cdp query unknowns
    $ cdp docs

`stats` is the shape, `routes` the outside edge, `unknowns` what to ask a human; `docs` writes `00-overview.md` under `<CDP_HOME>/work/<repo-slug>/docs/`.

### How two repos connect

_Service A calls service B; both are scanned._

    $ cdp scan
    $ cdp link scan --db
    $ cdp link query --service <repo-name>

`link scan --db` matches channel edges across every scanned repo in the machine store and saves them; `link query` lists a service's callers and unmatched calls.

### Refresh after commits

_The branch moved since the last scan._

    $ cdp status
    $ cdp refresh
    $ cdp query coverage

`refresh` re-verifies claims and re-extracts changed files with no model calls (use `scan` after large restructures); `status` shows behind/dirty; answers list uncommitted files they may not reflect.

### Review a change

_You need the blast radius of a diff._

    $ cdp query file <file>
    $ cdp query symbol <symbol>
    $ cdp diff --old-sha <sha> --new-sha <sha>

`file` + `symbol` give the touched definitions and their callers; `diff` shows structural deltas between two scanned snapshots.
